When you encounter these obstacles or questions on the path, first meet yourself with deep patience and warmth. The natural habit of the conditioned ego is to panic, resist, or frantically search for a technique to control present reality. But the Dhamma invites you to take a gentle step backward—to stop fighting the current moment and instead observe the unfolding process with calm, non-judgmental clarity.

When we look into the living reality of this teaching, the master points out with unwavering clarity: *"And then uh the senses themselves, you know, just my weak vision and poor hearing is is very much you realize sensory consciousness is very ephemeral, untrustworthy, and changeable. And then as you realize the emptiness of thoughts and memories and images, then you have the insight into pure consciousness or the deathless."* From the foundational perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering (*dukkha*) is never caused by the mere presence of sensations, thoughts, or external conditions.
